title: Module 0: Engineering maths, units and physical quantities
shortTitle: Engineering maths, units and physical quantities
whyItMatters: Almost every serious calculation error is either a wrong model, a wrong assumption, or a units/conversion error. You need units to feel automatic.
introduction: Establishes fluent metric SI unit conversions in the (mm, N) and (m, kN) systems, vector resolution by trigonometry, differential/integral relationships between load, shear, and bending moment, and clear physical distinctions between force, mass, stress, pressure, and stiffness.
objectives: Convert fluently between N, kN, MN, mm, m, mm², m², mm⁴, m⁴, kN/m, N/mm, kN/m², N/mm² (MPa), GPa, kg/m³, and kN/m³.
Rearrange structural equations, apply trigonometry and Pythagoras to inclined ties/struts, and interpret graph gradients and areas.
Distinguish mass vs weight, force vs stress, distributed load vs resultant point load, and stiffness vs strength.
learningGate: Convert all common structural units without hesitation.,Resolve inclined forces into orthogonal components without prompts.,Calculate moments of forces about a point correctly.,Replace a uniformly distributed load (UDL) with its equivalent resultant and line of action.,Check whether any structural equation is dimensionally sensible.

topics.title: Structural Units & Dimensional Homogeneity
topics.summary: Covers SI prefixes, area and second-moment-of-area unit powers, stress/modulus identities (1 MPa = 1 N/mm²), bending moment conversion (1 kN·m = 10⁶ N·mm), and dimensional checking.
subtopics: Force and length units: N, kN, MN; mm, m
Section geometry units: mm², m² (10⁶); mm³, cm³ (10³); mm⁴, cm⁴ (10⁴), m⁴ (10¹²)
Line load and surface pressure units: kN/m = N/mm; 1 kN/m² = 0.001 N/mm²
Stress and elastic modulus units: N/mm² = MPa; 1 GPa = 1,000 N/mm²
Unit weight vs mass density: kg/m³ and kN/m³ (using g = 9.81 m/s²)
learningObjectives: Convert bending moments, pressures, line loads, and section properties into consistent (mm, N) base units.
Spot 10³ and 10⁶ power-of-ten errors before they invalidate stress or deflection calculations.

questions.learningObjective: Convert elastic modulus from GPa to N/mm² (Example 0.1)
questions.prompt: Convert a structural steel Young’s modulus of E = 200 GPa into N/mm².
questions.assumptions: Assumes standard SI prefixes (1 GPa = 10³ MPa = 10³ N/mm²).
questions.explanation: 1 GPa = 10⁹ Pa = 1,000 MPa. Since 1 MPa = 1 N/mm², 200 GPa = 200 × 1,000 = 200,000 N/mm². Step-by-step verification for "Convert elastic modulus from GPa to N/mm² (Example 0.1)": confirm that all input quantities are converted into consistent SI metric units before substitution, evaluate the governing equilibrium or constitutive equation to obtain 200000 N/mm², and cross-check the magnitude and sign against StructTutor Syllabus Mod 0 (Units, Vectors & Equilibrium) & BS EN 1990 Basis of Structural Design.
questions.citation: BS EN 1990:2002+A1 Basis of Structural Design & SI Unit Conventions
hints: Identify the governing equilibrium or mechanics equation for "Convert elastic modulus from GPa to N/mm² (Example 0.1)" and convert all given dimensions and loads into consistent SI units (N, mm, or kN, m) before calculating.
Calculation setup: 1 GPa = 10⁹ Pa = 1,000 MPa. Express your final numeric answer in N/mm².

questions.learningObjective: Verify dimensional homogeneity of beam deflection equations
questions.prompt: In the standard elastic deflection formula δ = 5wL⁴ / (384EI), if w is in N/mm, L is in mm, E is in N/mm², and I is in mm⁴, what are the resulting units of δ?
questions.assumptions: Using consistent (mm, N) units guarantees δ emerges directly in mm without extra conversion factors.
options: Because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel
mm

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory

Because Eurocode partial safety factors for resistance incorporate a statistical log-normal coefficient of variation for hot-rolled plate thickness tolerances, mill rolling residual stresses, and out-of-straightness bow imperfections across the member length
questions.explanation: Numerator [w][L⁴] = (N/mm) × mm⁴ = N·mm³. Denominator [E][I] = (N/mm²) × mm⁴ = N·mm². Ratio = (N·mm³) / (N·mm²) = mm. Engineering synthesis for "Verify dimensional homogeneity of beam deflection equations": always trace the complete load path from point of application to the foundations, ensure compatibility between analysis boundary assumptions and physical site detailing, and verify against StructTutor Syllabus Mod 0 (Units, Vectors & Equilibrium) & BS EN 1990 Basis of Structural Design.
questions.citation: BS EN 1990:2002+A1 Basis of Structural Design & SI Unit Conventions
hints: Consider the physical load path, equilibrium boundary conditions, and deformation compatibility for "Verify dimensional homogeneity of beam deflection equations". Distinguish carefully between ULS strength/stability checks and SLS deflection/cracking behaviour.
Engineering principle check: eliminate options that violate static equilibrium, ignore construction-stage instability, or confuse elastic stiffness (E·I) with material yield strength (f_y).

questions.learningObjective: Use Pythagoras to determine inclined bracing length
questions.prompt: A temporary works raking shore spans a horizontal distance of 3.6 m and rises vertically 4.8 m to support a wall needle. What is the inclined length of the shore?
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras, L = √(3.6² + 4.8²) = √(12.96 + 23.04) = √36.0 = 6.0 m (a 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 1.2). questions.learningObjective: Interpret differential/integral meaning on shear and moment diagrams

It increases the elastic Euler critical buckling load by halving the effective buckling length between inflection points, provided that the connection detail transfers full axial thrust without slip or local web crippling

questions.learningObjective: Understand limitations of replacing a UDL with a single resultant point load
questions.prompt: When is it valid to replace a uniformly distributed load w over span L with a single concentrated load W = wL at midspan?
questions.assumptions: Crucial distinction between external equivalence and internal stress resultants.
options: When calculating the internal bending moment at midspan without restoring the distributed load on the free-body cut
When drawing the parabolic bending moment diagram as a triangular point-load diagram
When checking local web bearing at midspan where no point load physically exists
When writing global equilibrium equations to find external support reactions of a determinate beam
questions.explanation: Statically equivalent resultants preserve external global equilibrium (reactions), but internal shear V(x) and moment M(x) within the loaded region depend on the actual load distribution (wL²/8 for UDL vs WL/4 = wL²/4 for a midspan point load).
